agree.reason: The memo makes a clear, staged ask with checkpoints and a staffing plan the board will appreciate, but the ad-background members can still argue the case for keeping $84,000 of real money, because the memo understates how fast ads are falling and never shows that the pilot's pace already beats what the target needs.

honest.reason: The memo rightly softens 'will replace' to a stated goal and invents no numbers, but it says the $47,000 drop happened 'in two years' when it happened in one, and its $60,000–$67,000 projection rests on that mistake.

works_the_facts.reason: The pilot's annual value (~$20,000), its 1.5% conversion, and the targets of 875 and 680 members are all calculated correctly, but the memo misses the strongest number: 212 sign-ups in six weeks is about 35 a week, while 1,000 a year needs only about 19 a week.

right_comparison.reason: The memo does compare against keeping ads, but it treats a one-year 36% fall as a two-year trend, so the status quo looks better than it is (about $54,000 next year if the trend holds, not $60,000–$67,000).

qualification.reason: The June 30 checkpoint is checkable, with a number (400 members), a date and a consequence (options including sponsorships come back to the board); the retention and cash-gap points are still unfilled placeholders.

objections.reason: The memo deals with the long-serving ad salesperson and offers sponsorships as a fallback, which speaks to the sales-minded members, but the 'why give up $84,000 now' objection is only partly met and the cash-gap answer is left blank.

fit.reason: It is in proper memo form, ends with a motion, and runs to about one page, though the bracketed placeholders mean it isn't ready to send.
